stances.claim: Sara's own answer to her supporters is that she will be ready for 2028 -- but legally, under Article VII Section 8, she can still become president within 2022-2028 by VP succession if the elected president dies, becomes permanently disabled, is removed from office, or resigns, with Carlos P. Garcia (after Magsaysay) and GMA (after Estrada, via Estrada v. Desierto's 'totality of prior, contemporaneous and posterior facts and circumstantial evidence' doctrine) as the modern precedents.
stances.rhetorical_move: constitutional-precedent inventory (literal-text plus two precedents as the analytical core)

stances.claim: Under President Duterte's preferred scenario -- Bong Go (BG) wins the top post -- Duterte may urge BG to resign and give way to Sara, who can then run for a full 2028 reelection IF the unexpired BG term is less than four years (Article VII, Section 4); this parallels the Estrada/GMA precedent where Estrada constructively resigned on January 20, 2001 after just over two years, allowing GMA to serve over three years of the unexpired term plus her own 2004-2010 term -- making her the second-longest-serving president (9+ years) after Marcos's 21 and ahead of Quezon's 8.7.
stances.rhetorical_move: scenario-modeling-via-historical-parallel (GMA/Estrada timing as roadmap for the Sara/BG path)

stances.claim: However, Sara is now officially tandem with Bongbong, not BG -- and if Bongbong wins, 'I don't think he will give up the presidency. In fact, he may even frustrate Sara's wish to run in 2028 because, like his father, Bongbong may find ways to enable him to serve for more than six years,' making the constitutional-succession path improbable under the BBM scenario.
stances.rhetorical_move: father-analogy-as-prediction ('like his father... more than six years' invokes the Marcos extended-rule precedent)

stances.claim: President Duterte's parallel maneuvering -- Senate seat with Lakas-CMD support possibly snatching the Senate presidency, GMA running unopposed for Pampanga congressional seat and possibly returning as Speaker -- produces 'dynasties galore, we will in awe implore if they all score as the proud victors,' compounding the entrenchment risk.
stances.rhetorical_move: rhyming-mock-incantation register ('dynasties galore... implore... score') for dynastic critique

stances.claim: The opposition's best response is Sen. Ping Lacson's 'winningest-contenders' framework -- supporting the candidates topping credible polls. As of the SWS October 20-23 poll, that means Robredo (18%) at president and Sotto (44%) at VP, with Bongbong leading at 47% on the other side -- yielding a likely 'Bongbong-Sara versus Leni-Tito showdown.'
stances.rhetorical_move: poll-driven unity argument with concrete-numbers anchor (SWS data as decisional input)

stances.claim: Opposition unity by January 2022 'may be a bit late' because the winning candidates may have gained irreversible momentum by that time -- making the unity-now urgency the key strategic message of the column.

notable_anecdotes: CJ's Carlos-Garcia-after-Magsaysay reminder -- pairing it with GMA-after-Estrada-via-Estrada-v.-Desierto as the two modern VP-succession precedents -- a quiet historical-civics lesson embedded in a 2022-election scenario column.

The president-tenure ranking: Marcos 21 years (1965-1986), GMA 9-plus consecutive years (Jan 20, 2001 - June 30, 2010), Quezon 8.7 years (Nov 15, 1935 - Aug 1, 1944) -- one of CJ's most concise consolidated presidential-tenure histories.

The Bongbong/father analogy -- 'like his father, Bongbong may find ways to enable him to serve for more than six years' -- the most explicit single-line invocation of the Marcos extended-rule precedent in CJ's 2022-election columns, and the central reason Sara's 2028 path is constrained.

The rhyming verse 'Oh, dynasties galore, we will in awe implore if they all score as the proud victors' -- among the most stylistically distinctive lines in CJ's E-series columns, blending mock-incantation with dynasty critique.
The full SWS October 20-23, 2021 presidential and VP poll numbers preserved in the column -- making this column a useful data anchor for the late-November 2021 race state-of-play.

Sara's own pre-COC statement that she would 'be ready for the 2028 election' -- preserved as the column's framing-question setup and the answer Sara herself had already given, against which CJ then constructs the constitutional alternative.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban takes up the question repeatedly asked by Sara Duterte-Carpio's supporters after she filed her substitute COC for VP under Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo's Lakas-CMD: can Sara still become president before 2028? Sara herself had already said she would be ready for the 2028 election after six years -- but legally, under Article VII Section 8 of the Constitution, she can still become president within 2022-2028 if the elected president dies, becomes permanently disabled, is removed, or resigns, with two modern precedents: Carlos P. Garcia after Magsaysay's plane crash, and GMA after Estrada v. Desierto (March 2, 2001) held that the 'totality of prior, contemporaneous and posterior facts and circumstantial evidence' showed Estrada's constructive resignation. If President Duterte's preferred bet Sen. Bong Go wins the top post, Duterte may urge BG to resign and give way to a Sara presidency, with Sara eligible for a full 2028 reelection if BG's unexpired term is less than four years (Article VII Section 4) -- paralleling GMA's 9-plus consecutive years (second only to Marcos's 21 and ahead of Quezon's 8.7). However, Sara is now officially tandem with Bongbong, not BG, and if Bongbong wins, 'I don't think he will give up the presidency. In fact, he may even frustrate Sara's wish to run in 2028 because, like his father, Bongbong may find ways to enable him to serve for more than six years.' Meanwhile, Duterte is gunning for the Senate (possibly the Senate presidency via Lakas-CMD support) and GMA is running unopposed in Pampanga (possibly returning as Speaker), producing 'dynasties galore, we will in awe implore if they all score as the proud victors.' The opposition's best response is Sen. Ping Lacson's 'winningest-contenders' framework backed by the SWS October 20-23, 2021 poll (Bongbong 47%, Robredo 18%, Moreno 13%, Pacquiao 9%, Lacson and Dela Rosa tied at 5%; VP: Sotto 44%, Sara 25%) -- yielding a likely Bongbong-Sara versus Leni-Tito showdown. But the bets must not wait too long: unity by January 2022 'may be a bit late' because winning candidates may have gained irreversible momentum by then.
